title: Want to Sound More Confident Raise Your Eyebrows!
paragraphs: If you want to seem more confident when you speak, you may need to think about more than just your words and your voice. According to a new study, the movements of your eyebrows and eyes can also make a big difference.

The study was carried out by researchers at the University of Glasgow in Scotland and published in the journal Proceedings of the Royal Society B. It was led by Dr Jonas Nölle, a postdoctoral researcher at the university.

For the study, the researchers created computer-generated "speakers," who answered questions on a screen. They then changed the speakers' facial movements around the eyes and eyebrows. However, the speakers' words and tone of voice stayed exactly the same in every version.
Participants from Western European and East Asian cultures then watched and listened carefully to the different versions. They then rated how confident each of the answers seemed to them.

The results showed that facial movements had a significant effect on how confident the speakers seemed. Speakers who raised their eyebrows and briefly closed their eyes were seen as more confident. On the other hand, speakers who lowered their eyebrows and narrowed their eyes seemed doubtful or less confident. Interestingly, people from both cultural groups reacted in a similar way.

Nölle explained that when people listen to someone speak, they pay attention to more than just the words and the voice. Professor Rachael Jack, another researcher involved in the study, added that raising the eyebrows and closing the eyes were linked with greater confidence across different cultures.

These findings could be useful in many situations where people can see each other, such as job interviews, presentations and video calls. So, the next time you want to sound sure of yourself, try raising your eyebrows. It may help other people believe what you are saying.
